Arditi.fact: Satisfied with the Bersaglieri Assault Company, Capello asked Cadorna for permission to create an assault unit with regular infantry soldiers and the Generalissimo granted it.

Arditi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy

Arditi.question: In the early hours of 19 _____ the entire Company was on the other side and at dawn the attack on Loga began

Arditi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Arditi.question: Despite this, Loga was secured and the "_____" Brigade had crossed the Isonzo so the Assault Company had done its duty
Arditi.fact: Despite this, Loga was secured and the "Trapani" Brigade had crossed the Isonzo so the Assault Company had done its duty.

Arditi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy

Arditi.fact: Having easily conquered the front line trenches parallel to the river, Radicati's Company pushed deep into the town and, leaving a platoon to mop up the buildings, clashed against a railway toll booth defended by numerically superior enemies who pushed back the Arditi. Arditi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Arditi.question: In the early hours of _____ 19, the 2nd Company ran across the bridge under fire and found itself on the other side with its entire force
Arditi.fact: Remaining on the front line until the morning of August 20, the unit returned to Ronzina and from there by truck to Kambresko. Arditi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Arditi.question: The following day they returned to _____ where they rejoined the 1st Company
Arditi.fact: The following day they returned to Kambresko where they rejoined the 1st Company.

Arditi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Arditi.question: South of Loga, the 4th _____ operated and was attached to the 21st Bersaglieri Regiment of the V Bersaglieri Brigade which, with the I Bersaglieri Brigade, formed the 47th Division
Arditi.fact: The following day they returned to Kambresko where they rejoined the 1st Company. South of Loga, the 4th Company operated and was attached to the 21st Bersaglieri Regiment of the V Bersaglieri Brigade which, with the I Bersaglieri Brigade, formed the 47th Division.

Arditi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy

Arditi.fact: The Division was tasked with breaking through the first enemy defensive line on the Bainsizza, consisting of three fortified hills: Fratta, Semmer and height 856.

Arditi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy

Arditi.fact: The Company commanded by Captain Salvadori began the crossing at 11pm on August 18 and by midnight was completely on the other bank south of Loga. The Brigade reorganized and the 4th Company was attached to the XXXVII Bersaglieri Battalion.

Arditi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Arditi.question: The next day the _____ attacked the Fratta with the Assault Company in the lead and managed to occupy the top of the hill
Arditi.fact: The Brigade reorganized and the 4th Company was attached to the XXXVII Bersaglieri Battalion. The next day the Battalion attacked the Fratta with the Assault Company in the lead and managed to occupy the top of the hill.

Arditi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Arditi.question: In the meantime, the Semmer and height _____ were also occupied by the I Bersaglieri Brigade and the first Austro-Hungarian line was broken
Arditi.fact: In the meantime, the Semmer and height 856 were also occupied by the I Bersaglieri Brigade and the first Austro-Hungarian line was broken.

Arditi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy

Arditi.fact: The next day the Battalion attacked the Fratta with the Assault Company in the lead and managed to occupy the top of the hill. More difficult was the debut of the 3rd Assault Company which was sent much further south near Gorizia under the command of the 48th Division.

Arditi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy

Arditi.fact: After the clashes on Bainsizza and on the hills east of Gorizia, the four companies gathered at Sdricca to prepare the action that Capello had in mind. In fact, after the breakthrough of the Austro-Hungarian lines on Bainsizza, the Italian army crashed against Mount San Gabriele.

Arditi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Arditi.question: In fact, after the breakthrough of the Austro-_____ lines on Bainsizza, the Italian army crashed against Mount San Gabriele
Arditi.fact: In fact, after the breakthrough of the Austro-Hungarian lines on Bainsizza, the Italian army crashed against Mount San Gabriele.

Arditi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Arditi.question: The first attack was launched on August _____ by troops of the "Arno" Brigade who briefly occupied the peak before being repelled by a counterattack
Arditi.fact: The first attack was launched on August 31 by troops of the "Arno" Brigade who briefly occupied the peak before being repelled by a counterattack.

Arditi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Arditi.question: Capello immediately decided to use the 2nd, 3rd and 4th companies under the command of _____, who in the meantime had been placed in charge of the entire I Battalion
Arditi.fact: Capello immediately decided to use the 2nd, 3rd and 4th companies under the command of Maggiorino Radicati, who in the meantime had been placed in charge of the entire I Battalion.

Arditi.fact: The 4th Company took Santa Caterina and the positions behind it, linking up with the 2nd on the eastern slopes.

Arditi.fact: From Sabotino, Cadorna, Capello and King Vittorio Emanuele watched Lieutenant Salvatore Farina plant the tricolour on San Gabriele using a captured rifle as a spear.

Arditi.fact: In the following days the mountain changed occupant several times following attacks and counterattacks from both sides until on 10 September the Italians gave up and left San Gabriele in enemy hands.

Arditi.fact: The task was to advance in succession on Heights 145, 175, 199, 279 and 280 along the Flondar-Medeazza line.

Arditi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Arditi.question: The Italians continued towards _____ 175 but, due to the lack of officers and cohesion, the assault unit disintegrated and the companies fought separately and isolated
Arditi.fact: The task was to advance in succession on Heights 145, 175, 199, 279 and 280 along the Flondar-Medeazza line. After the artillery barrage, the Arditi, followed by the battalions of the "Murge" Brigade, went over the top at 8 am against Height 145 which was taken at 09:45 am.

Arditi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy

Arditi.fact: Only the 1st Company of the I Battalion escaped encirclement and managed to rejoin Bassi's Battalions, which were now among the few units of the 2nd Army that had not disintegrated.

Arditi.fact: On the Asiago Plateau, where the 11th Austro-Hungarian Army was pressing, three of the four Assault Battalions of the 1st Italian Army threw themselves into the fray.

Arditi.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy

Arditi.fact: The IX Assault Battalion of the 1st Army was disbanded, in addition to losses, also for serious acts of indiscipline committed in November and its still able men were integrated into the XVI Assault Battalion while the others were expelled from the Arditi Corp. The XVIII Battalion of the Carnia Zone and the V of the 4th Army were also disbanded for losses and their men integrated into the VI Assault Battalion.

ArmSCII.question: The _____ was Set of obsolete single-byte character encodings.
ArmSCII.fact: ArmSCII or ARMSCII is a set of obsolete single-byte character encodings for the Armenian alphabet defined by Armenian national standard 166–9. ArmSCII is an acronym for Armenian Standard Code for Information Interchange, similar to ASCII for the American standard.

ArmSCII.question: It has been superseded by the _____ standard
ArmSCII.fact: It has been superseded by the Unicode standard. ArmSCII.fact: However, this encoding cannot map all the punctuation characters normally needed for Armenian, so the missing characters must be approximated using fallbacks to ASCII punctuation (some Armenian fonts may display these ASCII punctuation using the rendering intended for the Armenian characters that are mapped to them by these fallbacks). Berhe has delivered 200+ invited talks worldwide, including two TED Talks, related to soil science, biogeochemistry and nature-based climate change solutions at the White House, Congressional hearings, and more.
